meta.title: Correlation registry — pairs, triples and player-prop combos
meta.principle: A correlation is only allowed on the site if it is either (a) computed from verified data by scripts/compute_correlation.py, or (b) declared as an assumption with its mechanism and a pending-verification badge. No correlation is ever asserted as fact without one of those two labels.
meta.r_squared_note: r^2 is the share of variance in the outcome explained by the input. It is reported so strategy sizing can be honest about how much is unexplained.
meta.sign_convention: Positive = the two legs win together more often than chance. Negative = one leg winning makes the other less likely (hedge).

measured.label: Team win percentage vs point differential per game
measured.interpretation: Most of win percentage is explained by scoring margin. The remaining 22.9% of variance is where one-score luck lives — that is exactly what the LUCK-FILTER gate strips.
measured.use: Justifies using point differential as the primary rating input and treating raw W-L as a noisy secondary.

measured.label: Team win percentage vs points scored per game
measured.interpretation: Offence alone explains under half of win percentage. Offence-only strategies must therefore carry a wider band.
measured.use: Sets the minimum evidence bar: an offence-only signal needs more games before it is allowed to size.

measured.label: Team win percentage vs points allowed per game
measured.interpretation: Defence explains slightly less of win percentage than offence, and it is not a mirror image of offence.
measured.use: Defence-only signals get a wider band and a higher evidence bar, same as offence.

measured.label: Points scored per game vs points allowed per game
measured.interpretation: Offence and defence are close to independent across clubs. This is the single most important correlation fact for parlay construction: a 'good offence' leg and a 'bad defence' leg on the SAME club are nearly independent, so stacking them does not multiply risk as violently as intuition suggests — but it also does not create free correlation the way a same-game script does.
measured.use: Blocks the naive parlay of 'team scores a lot' + 'team allows a lot' being treated as a hedge.

assumed.label: Same-game: home spread and total
assumed.mechanism: A blowout can come from a fast start (raises total) or a shutdown (lowers it). Margin and total have no monotone link.
assumed.pending: Needs game-level historical results to measure. Not captured in this build.
assumed.sizing_implication: Treat as independent for now, but do not let one leg exceed 1/2 of the parlay weight.

assumed.label: Same-game: QB passing yards + team total points
assumed.mechanism: Passing volume drives scoring, but a trailing team passes more while scoring is already set, and a leading team runs out the clock.
assumed.pending: Needs player-level official stats per game.
assumed.sizing_implication: Positive correlation inflates the joint probability; any pricing that treats the legs independently will overstate the payout edge.

assumed.label: Same-game: RB rushing yards + team spread (team winning)
assumed.mechanism: Leading teams run more; a run-heavy script is a consequence of leading, which is the same event as covering.
assumed.pending: Needs play-level or game-level rushing splits from an official source.
assumed.sizing_implication: This is the strongest known correlation family in NFL props. Do not stack RB rushing overs with opponent-spread legs.

assumed.label: Same-game: WR receiving yards + QB passing yards
assumed.mechanism: Shared targets. If the WR hits, the QB very likely hit.
assumed.sizing_implication: Stacking these two as independent legs is close to betting the same event twice. Gate PARLAY-IND requires an explicit shared-driver declaration.

assumed.label: Cross-game parlay legs (different games, different clubs)
assumed.mechanism: No shared players, no shared clock, no shared weather. The only shared term is league-wide scoring environment, which is a level, not an outcome.
assumed.pending: None — independence is structural. Residual correlation from shared league conditions is small and is absorbed by the parlay haircut.
assumed.sizing_implication: Multipliers are still cut, because a shared league-wide shock (e.g. a scoring boom) hits every over simultaneously.

assumed.label: Availability-driven change in the same game (starter out -> total and spread)
assumed.sign: directional, sign depends on side of the ball
assumed.mechanism: A missing starter on offence lowers that club's scoring; on defence it raises the opponent's scoring. Both move the spread the same way; the total moves in OPPOSITE directions.
assumed.pending: The engine applies this causally (scripts/compute_lines.py) but the magnitude is a declared constant, not measured.
assumed.sizing_implication: Do not treat 'player out' as automatically 'under'. This registry exists specifically to block that heuristic.

parlay_rules.rule: Never price a parlay by multiplying legs unless every shared driver is listed.
parlay_rules.why: r(A4) between QB and WR yardage legs is close to 1 in mechanism, so naive multiplication exaggerates the payout.

parlay_rules.rule: Cap same-game legs at 2 per ticket in v0.
parlay_rules.why: Every additional same-game leg adds an unmeasured correlation term. Two legs is the most we can decompose with the evidence we hold.

parlay_rules.rule: Apply a haircut equal to the largest unmeasured correlation term in the ticket.
parlay_rules.why: Conservative pricing. The haircut is shown on the leaderboard so the cost of uncertainty is visible rather than hidden.

parlay_rules.rule: Cross-game legs must come from games played on different days OR different clubs; same-club, different-game is impossible by definition.
parlay_rules.why: Structural independence (COR-A5) only holds if no player or club is shared.

unmeasurable_now.what: Any correlation involving a market price
unmeasurable_now.why: No licensed official odds feed (flag F07). Correlations between our line and the market's line cannot be computed because we do not hold the market's line.
Official per-game player statistics were not captured in this build. COR-A2/A3/A4 remain assumptions with magnitude unverified.
